plans.hypothesis: A two-segment arm with four equally spaced full-span tendons and identical positive payout offsets will remain compliant and effectively slack at low loads, while the tendon on the extending side will engage under each opposite high-load bend, producing approximately symmetric progressive stiffness for plus-x and minus-x.
plans.interpretation: This is a new unmeasured structure designed to test delayed unilateral engagement, not a claim of task success. Fourfold symmetry is intended to remove a directional confounder; the common positive payout offset is the primary engagement-delay intervention.
plans.stopping_condition: Stop this design branch if it cannot produce a qualified unloaded state or bilateral delayed activation under current scoped analysis; otherwise proceed to candidate-bound mechanism diagnosis and then a matched physical evaluation before any validation replay.

plans.hypothesis: Candidate 68's common 0.0008 m payout offsets create an unloaded slack active set, while opposing full-span tendons engage under plus-x and minus-x loading strongly enough to increase late-stage stiffness without suppressing low-stage displacement.
plans.interpretation: This diagnosis tests the generated delayed-engagement mechanism. Candidate compilation is a numerical fact; unloaded slack, bilateral activation, progressive stiffness, and task acceptance remain hypotheses.
plans.stopping_condition: If unloaded qualification fails, revise the structure rather than infer finite-time infeasibility. If unloaded slack is qualified, proceed to a complete paired finite-time baseline/ablation on selected real tendons before considering independent replay.

plans.hypothesis: Reducing the common tendon payout offset from 0.0008 m to 0.0004 m while reducing both circular segment radii from 0.006 m to 0.0059 m will preserve unloaded slack, increase low-stage displacement above 0.006 m, and permit symmetric tendon engagement at high load, producing progressive stiffness in both load directions without exceeding the high-displacement bound.
plans.interpretation: Result_2 numerically establishes bilateral non-engagement, stiffness ratios near 0.9955, low displacement near 0.005761 m, passing high-displacement bounds, and no contacts for candidate_68. The payout and radius causal attribution and the chosen edit are hypotheses. Generation itself will not establish task performance or physical acceptance.
plans.stopping_condition: After compilation, diagnose the new candidate and run one complete paired finite-time baseline/ablation using selected real tendon entities. If it fails, use the measured mechanism pattern to choose a further bounded edit or topology change; do not infer global infeasibility.

plans.hypothesis: Candidate 294's 0.0004 m common payout offsets will allow the symmetric real tendons to remain slack at low load but engage at high load in both directions, while the 0.0059 m segment radii will raise low-stage displacement above 0.006 m; compared with matched ablation of all four tendons, engagement will produce the required progressive-stiffness contrast without violating high-displacement, recovery, contact, or stability limits.
plans.interpretation: Numerical facts from result_2 are that candidate_68 was complete and symmetric but did not engage, had stiffness ratios about 0.9955, low displacement about 0.005761 m, passed high-displacement and no-contact limits, and remained scientifically unaccepted. Candidate_294 compilation and its six edited leaves are facts. Delayed engagement, improved low displacement, progressive stiffness, and ablation contrast for candidate_294 remain hypotheses.

With compliant circular sections and small positive payout offsets, direction-appropriate tendons may remain slack at low load and become taut at high load while preserving bilateral symmetry.

plans.hypothesis: Candidate 745's invalid finite-time observation is dominated by insufficient material damping rather than route illegality or failure of unloaded equilibrium. Raising both bending-viscosity axes uniformly on all four segments from 0.0004 to the registered upper bound of 0.0007 N*m^2*s, while preserving topology, stiffness, routing, payout and mass, should reduce the symmetric persistent motion enough to qualify the frozen stage windows and reveal whether the existing unilateral tendons provide genuine high-load progressive stiffening.
plans.interpretation: Numerical facts from result_6: unloaded equilibrium was qualified, checked routes were legal and contact count was zero; all six stage windows failed tip-speed, monitor-speed, generalized-velocity, tail-drift, static-balance and length-excess checks; bidirectional tail drift increased from about 0.000970 m at low stage to 0.001822 m at middle stage and 0.002826 m at high stage; high displacement was about 0.032624 m and exceeded 0.025 m. Hypothesis: uniformly increased material viscosity will suppress the common unsettled response without materially changing static compliance. Reporter interpretation that the pattern is consistent with inadequate damping is contextual, not a numerical fact or causal proof.

plans.hypothesis: The damping-only intervention is weakened by result_7: increasing all bending viscosities to their registered ceiling did not qualify any stage and increased tail drift relative to result_6. A moderate, uniform increase in elastic modulus is now the higher-information structural intervention. Raising all four segments from 7.0 MPa to 9.5 MPa should reduce the approximately 0.03239 m high-stage displacement below 0.025 m and shorten settling, while the observed low-stage displacement margin of approximately 0.00836 m may remain above 0.006 m. Preserving the distributed tendon routing and payout keeps the later slack-to-taut mechanism test interpretable.
plans.interpretation: Numerical facts: result_7 preserved qualified unloaded equilibrium, legal checked routes, zero contacts, and bilateral low displacement near 0.00836 m, but bilateral high displacement was near 0.03239 m and every stage failed six dynamic checks. Its low, middle, and high tail drifts were approximately 0.00119, 0.00207, and 0.00413 m, worse than result_6 despite maximum registered viscosity. Hypothesis: a uniform modulus increase to 9.5 MPa can trade the observed compliance margin for lower high-load displacement and faster settling without changing the tendon geometry. Reporter interpretation that the response is unsettled is contextual and does not prove this cause. Hard static equilibrium remains eligibility evidence only and cannot establish finite-time or physical acceptance.
